intent: Edit the existing surface maps using approved v4 concepts as style references.

green.prompt: Production game texture edit. Image 1 is the target equirectangular cloud surface map. Image 2 is approved style and palette reference only; do not copy its UI, stars or ships. Make a new seamless 2:1 rectangular full-surface gas giant ALBEDO map, maximum available resolution, ideally 4096x2048. Keep image 1's emerald/forest/olive/chartreuse palette, but replace its overly broad soft belts and huge vortices with MUCH FINER sharply painted cloud forms matching reference 2. This texture will be heavily magnified: only about ONE TENTH of map width is visible across the game's planet. Put 18-24 distinct oval cyclone systems around the whole map, each roughly 3-5 percent of map width, connected by many narrow flowing bands, scalloped eddies, crisp nested brush shapes, fine turbulent contour lines. Several contrasting emerald green levels, muted yellow-green accents occupying small areas, jewel dark-green shadows. Painterly cel-painted graphic cloud contours, with distinct color boundaries like reference 2; avoid blurry noise, airbrush, repetitive identical spirals, and wide featureless smears. All parts have equal uniform illumination; no baked lighting, no large vignette, no terminator or side shadow. Fill entire rectangle with continuous unwrapped cloud surface. No circular planet, no hemisphere shape, no space or stars, no rim, no atmosphere, no typography, no transparency. Horizontal wrap must be seamless. Keep extreme polar rows quiet. Preserve saturated character without neon yellow or pale washed-out mint. The main change is finer sharply defined surface detail, not globally brighter output.

blue.prompt: Production game texture edit. Image 1 is the equirectangular surface map to refine; image 2 is approved cobalt planet style reference only. Output one full-rectangle seamless 2:1 latitude-longitude ALBEDO texture, maximum resolution ideally4096x2048. Preserve rich midnight blue, cobalt and ultramarine palette of reference2 with narrow medium azure highlights. Replace target's excessively wide soft bands and gigantic soft storms with finer very clearly painted cloud contours, small hook-shaped eddies, narrow sweeping jet streams and 12-18 varied tightly curled cyclone systems distributed across the surface, approximately4-6 percent of total map width each. A visible hemisphere in-game shows only ONE TENTH of map width, so intricate crisp nested brush shapes are essential. More long swirling ribbons and fewer circular bullseyes than a Jupiter map; each storm different. Stylized cel-painted cloud brushwork matching reference2, deliberately clear hard color boundaries and little fine atmospheric striation, not photographic noise and not airbrushed gradients. Keep quiet deep navy areas between azure ribbons; no global brightening, no lavender, no gray desaturation, no white cloud masses. Uniform even illumination across surface, no baked directional light, no day/night shadow, no rim, no vignette. Entire image must be flat unwrapped cloud texture, NOT a picture of a sphere. No stars, space, background, ships, UI, typography, transparency or perspective. Left/right edges tile seamlessly, polar rows quiet. This is a more detailed replacement for target1 with the same palette, intended for independent spherical lighting in engine.
